newsitem.title: USA: Cohen says U.S.troops ready for Zaire evacuations.
newsitem.headline: Cohen says U.S.troops ready for Zaire evacuations.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Monday that 219 U.S. troops were on standby near Zaire to evacuate American citizens and more than 600 troops should be in the area by Tuesday.
"There has been no request for an evacuation at this time and we stand at the ready to respond if necessary," Cohen told reporters.

Another 1,000 Marines were heading for the region aboard the helicopter landing ship Nassau, which helped to evacuate Americans from Albania. Defence officials said it would take the ship about 10 days to arrive in the area.
"The ship has been ordered to move to the area (and be) on standby," one said.
Other U.S. defence officials said the 219 American troops were in Brazzaville, in the Congo and Libreville, Gabon.
The State Department said about 650 Americans had been living in Zaire, most of them in the capital Kinshasa. By Friday, the number was down to about 500.
The United States, France and Belgium put troops in position to evacuate their citizens as President Mobutu Sese Seko tried to defuse a rebel drive to topple him.
